page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The underlying Intel processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) for accelerated matrix operations, and hardware-assisted cryptography via AES and SHA_NI. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching top-tier status at 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression performing strongly at 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-core and write-heavy workloads show relative limitations; stress-ng multi-core performance and large-block memory write bandwidth (23.77 GB/sec) fall into the lower performance tier. General database operations, Redis SET performance (8.24 million operations per second), and static web serving throughput (8.72 GB/sec) maintain average tier rankings.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring fast single-core execution and local high-speed scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The combination of dedicated compute, local NVMe storage, and advanced matrix instructions makes this instance well-suited for general-purpose workloads, lightweight database hosting, static web serving, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
